items.headline: Vercel April 2026 security incident
items.summary: Vercel was breached in April 2026 when attackers compromised Context.ai, a third-party AI productivity tool, via Lumma Stealer malware in February with a two-month dwell time. The attackers used OAuth access to take over a Vercel employee's Google Workspace account, pivoted into Vercel's internal environment, and exfiltrated non-sensitive environment variables for a subset of customers. The incident exposes the supply chain risk of small AI productivity tools with broad OAuth permissions.
items.levelshiftAngle: This incident validates the AI governance and third-party risk management components in LevelShift's 5-Phase Value Realization Framework, particularly Phase 4 Architecture & Enablement. Our SOC 2 certification and governance playbooks position us to help clients audit their AI tool stack for OAuth sprawl and shadow AI risks before procurement enforces restrictions. This is a direct sales talking point for Financial Services and Healthcare clients subject to strict vendor risk management requirements. Add this case study to the AI governance workshop deck and use it to open conversations about AI supply chain security.

items.headline: EU AI Act Compliance Guide - Updated June 2026
items.summary: The EU AI Act becomes fully enforceable on August 2, 2026, making the EU the first jurisdiction with comprehensive AI regulation. Key compliance deadline for most organizations is August 2, 2026, though the EU AI Act Omnibus extended Annex III high-risk systems to December 2, 2027. Penalties reach up to 35 million euros or 7% of global annual turnover for violations. High-risk systems must satisfy obligations spanning risk management, data governance, technical documentation, transparency, human oversight, and cybersecurity.
